objective: Apply logarithm rules with valid domains and solve exponential or logarithmic equations with complete solution checks.
assessmentPolicy: Thirty-four named variants supply independent practice. Four mixed critical checkpoint items sample one question per family. All four selected items must pass without assistance. A passed sample does not claim that every named variant was checked.

coverage.skill: Preserve both values and allowed inputs
instruction: Preserve both values and allowed inputs
examples: Equal on a shared domain is not full equivalence
An absolute value preserves both branches
coverage.retrieval: Give an input that distinguishes two domains, then repair the rewrite using an absolute value.

examples: A product becomes a sum of logarithms
A quotient keeps its order
Two negative factors cannot be split into real logs
coverage.retrieval: Derive a product and a quotient rule from exponent arithmetic, then test a pair of negative factors against the hypotheses.

coverage.skill: Move powers and roots with their conditions
instruction: Move powers and roots with their conditions
examples: A negative power is a signed multiplier
A root contributes a reciprocal exponent
coverage.retrieval: Derive the power identity and apply it to one negative exponent and one positive root.

coverage.skill: Expand even powers over the full real domain
instruction: Expand even powers over the full real domain
examples: Expand a quotient of even powers
An odd power keeps a positivity requirement
coverage.retrieval: Expand a quotient with two different even powers and explain every excluded input and every absolute value.

coverage.skill: Condense on the original common domain
instruction: Condense on the original common domain
examples: Condense coefficients into a single rational argument
The condensed formula can accept extra inputs
coverage.retrieval: Condense a variable expression, then inspect an extra input accepted by the new formula but excluded by the original logarithms.

coverage.skill: Keep restrictions after cancellation and multiplication by zero
instruction: Keep restrictions after cancellation and multiplication by zero
examples: Cancellation keeps an excluded point
A zero multiplier does not define a logarithm
coverage.retrieval: Simplify a canceled factor and a zero coefficient while retaining the original domain in each result.

coverage.skill: Disprove false sum rules and repair mixed bases
instruction: Disprove false sum rules and repair mixed bases
examples: A counterexample to a logarithm sum rule
An accidental match is not an identity
Convert a different base before combining
coverage.retrieval: Give both an exact counterexample and an accidental agreement for a false sum rule, then repair a different-base combination.

coverage.skill: Change base and separate exact from approximate results
instruction: Change base and separate exact from approximate results
examples: Keep an exact quotient and a separate decimal
A reciprocal base changes the sign
coverage.retrieval: Derive the change-of-base quotient, compute a reciprocal-base sign, and separate an exact expression from its rounded report.

examples: Use a common reciprocal base
Rewrite related bases before equating exponents
coverage.retrieval: Solve a reciprocal-base equality and a related-base equality, checking the complete original exponents.

coverage.skill: Isolate a shifted exponential before taking logarithms
instruction: Isolate a shifted exponential before taking logarithms
examples: Isolate a shifted exponential with a negative coefficient
A zero exponential target has no solution
A negative exponential target has no solution
coverage.retrieval: Isolate a shifted exponential with a negative scale, then explain separate zero-target and negative-target failures.

examples: Solve an equation with the natural base
Take logarithms when the bases differ
coverage.retrieval: Solve one natural exponential and one different-base equality, keeping the coefficient and constant logarithms exact.

examples: An exponential identity keeps every real input
Canceled x terms can leave a contradiction
coverage.retrieval: Classify one identity and one contradiction after the x terms disappear, stating the complete original solution set.

coverage.skill: Use a quadratic substitution with u greater than zero
instruction: Use a quadratic substitution with u greater than zero
examples: Two positive substitution roots give two solutions
Reject a negative substitution root and keep the positive one
Zero and negative substitution candidates can leave no solution
A repeated positive root gives one distinct input
coverage.retrieval: State the range of u=b^x before solving, then classify two positive roots, one retained root, no retained roots and a repeated positive root.
